Hi Samantha / team —

Thanks for the questions — below is a concise technical summary. Happy to expand in the SE call.

1) Control plane topology options
   - Hosted-managed control plane (minimal customer egress): control-plane signals are outbound TLS to Redwood's control endpoints for metrics/rollouts. Model payloads (inference) remain in-customer VPC when using Private mode via private peering (no model weights leave VPC). This requires an outbound HTTPS allowlist for the control-plane endpoints.
   - Customer-managed control plane (VPC-only): we can deploy the control plane into your account (no external control-plane egress). This is our recommended setup for regulated customers who require no persistent external metadata flow.

2) Fully air-gapped feasibility
   - Fully air-gapped: feasible in our on-prem package but with operational caveats: model updates, security patches, and runtime optimizations require an offline bundle that your ops team imports during maintenance windows. No outbound telemetry by default; audit logs are stored locally.
   - Hybrid: tokenization + sensitive preprocessing can remain on-prem while model weights are fetched from a secure staging network during scheduled windows; reduces operational overhead but does require controlled egress during maintenance windows.

3) Hyperscaler comparison (high level)
   - Latency: hyperscaler endpoints may have lower single-request latency if co-located, but Redwood’s optimized runtime + KV cache narrows that gap for conversational flows.
   - Cost & unit economics: hyperscaler managed endpoints often incur higher per-inference costs and additional maintenance for autoscaling policies; Redwood's batching + prefix caching reduces per-token cost in steady state.
   - Operator effort: hyperscaler = more ops (model packaging, autoscaling rules, kernel tuning). Redwood Private = lower day-to-day ops, we handle runtime upgrades (or provide offline bundles for air-gapped), and provide rollout primitives.

4) Proposed perf test matrix (we can run these in your account or a test VPC):
   - Scenario A: chat (1000 short conversations): measure P50/P95/P99 latency and tokens per second.
   - Scenario B: batch embeddings (10k docs): measure throughput & cost per embedding.
   - Scenario C: KV-cache heavy generation (prefix reuse): measure cost and latency after warm cache.

Deliverables: CSV of raw latency samples, aggregated PCTLs, cost model comparison vs a listed hyperscaler SKU, and a short write-up of network requirements for each topology.

I’ll propose times for a call (I have windows Fri 12–14 PDT and Mon 09–12 PDT).

- Rishi
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Short answers on the compliance/data-evidence front: 

- SOC2: we can share a redacted SOC2 summary and control mappings today. Attached: SOC2-summary-2025.pdf (redacted).
- KMS/HSM: Redwood Private integrates with customer KMS for key wrapping and supports BYOK for on-prem deployments.

Air-gapped specifics: for fully air-gapped deployments we provide an offline artifacts bundle that contains runtime binaries, model shard packages (if you request a model weight snapshot), and a scripted installer.
